newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Manila overnight money jumps on rate hike.
newsitem.headline: Manila overnight money jumps on rate hike.

text.p: *Traders say rates may stay high for some time

Manila overnight money jumped to an average of 11.0625 percent on Friday from 10.28125 after the Central Bank raised its overnight borrowing rate by 0.75 percentage points to 11 percent late Wednesday, traders said.
Banks were closed for a holiday on Thursday.
The Central Bank was forced to lift its rate as a pre-emptive move against peso speculation over fears of possible large outflows from stock market sales.
Dollars continue to depart despite the Central Bank's move on rates to calm the foreign exchange market, traders said.
That could again prod the Central Bank to raise its rates, traders said.
A Reuter poll of six financial institutions gave offer rates of 10.40 to 10.90 percent on the three-month bills; 10.65 to 11.25 percent on the six months; and 11.40 to 11.50 on the one-year bills.
